## Overview
DAAK_TECH is a French-language public technology-services/portfolio marketing website, not an authenticated SaaS product. The checked-out runtime is Next.js App Router + React/TypeScript (`package.json`: Next 16.4.3, React 19.2.8; exact installed versions need dependency-agent verification), Tailwind styling, and a Node-runtime contact handler. `next.config.ts:4` requests standalone output. Product code lives in `src/app`, `src/components`, `src/data`, and `src/lib`; static media in `public`. `assets`, `.agents/.claude/.cursor/.devin` skills, `venv`, and generated `strix_runs` are tooling/assets rather than additional deployed applications. `src/app(public)` is outside the actual `src/app` routing root and appears to be legacy duplicate content. README is create-next-app boilerplate, CLAUDE.md delegates to AGENTS.md, and no SECURITY.md was identified. Root AGENTS.md requires consulting installed Next.js docs before code edits.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
Anonymous visitors may read all marketing pages and submit contact inquiries. No login, role, tenant, cookie/session implementation, database access, admin handler, or auth middleware was found in `src`; `robots.ts:11` mentioning `/admin/` does not establish such a route. Slugs select public developer-maintained records, not private user objects. Developer-controlled `src/data/services.ts` and `src/data/projects.ts` supply service/project descriptions, URLs, and media paths. Operator-controlled `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, and `CONTACT_EMAIL` are loaded only by `src/lib/email/contact-email.ts:43-50` and authorize the server's external email service.

Attacker-controlled inputs are `/services/[slug]` and `/realisations/[slug]` path slugs; the `/contact?service=` query preselection; all multipart body fields and attachment bytes/name/type sent to `POST /api/contact`; and general HTTP metadata. The principal mutable boundary is anonymous HTTP input -> server validation and MIME/extension/size checks -> Resend email API -> internal team mailbox and requester-provided confirmation recipient. Contact PII and files are intended for the team, not public retrieval. Privacy disclosure (`src/app/(public)/politique-confidentialite/page.tsx:37-40`) says attachments are emailed and not retained on the site's server, consistent with the current route. `savePrivateAttachment` is present in `src/lib/files/al-private-storage.ts` but no imports/callers were found; it is not the live contact path. Runtime/deployment exposure and reverse-proxy protections are unverified; no remote production targets are in this task's scope.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
Observed source routes: GET `/`, `/services`, `/services/[slug]`, `/realisations`, `/realisations/[slug]`, `/a-propos`, `/contact`, `/mentions-legales`, `/politique-confidentialite`, `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, and `GET /api/health` (`src/app/api/health/route.ts:4`); `POST /api/contact` (`src/app/api/contact/route.ts:98`). Config redirects `/about-us` -> `/a-propos` and `/contact-us` -> `/contact`. Framework-generated static/media/image handling must be verified against the installed Next.js runtime separately.

Contact flow: browser client `src/components/forms/contact-form.tsx:204-311` performs Zod validation, builds FormData, and fetches `/api/contact`. Server route checks multipart content type (`:113`), fully parses FormData (`:137`), short-circuits a nonempty `website` honeypot (`:146-167`), extracts explicit scalar fields, and calls `contactServerSchema.safeParse` (`:228`). Server schema bounds names/contact strings/message, validates email, and restricts `service` to static service slugs (`src/lib/validation/contact-server.ts:11-89`). Single `attachment` field is checked for <=4 MiB (`route.ts:284`), allowlisted extension (`:307`) and declared MIME if nonempty (`:338`), then converted to base64 (`:363-382`) without saving or parsing document contents. Email sink `sendContactEmails` (`route.ts:391`) uses fixed operator-controlled internal recipient (`contact-email.ts:82`), user email as replyTo (`:84`), and sends a second confirmation to user email (`:246-251`). HTML interpolations pass through local five-character `escapeHtml` (`:23-29`); subject's service name comes from static data. No application-level rate limit, origin validation, CAPTCHA, idempotency key, or total-body preparse bound was observed in this route; these are risk surfaces requiring consequence-based validation, not confirmed findings.

Priority attacker stories: abuse publicly reachable email sending/recipient confirmation and repeated submissions; malformed/oversized multipart handling before postparse checks; filename/MIME/extension interpretation at email boundary; HTML/header injection despite existing escaping and SDK validation; error-path sensitivity and accidental config/secret exposure. Service/project slug resolution uses static data plus `notFound()` for absent records (`services/[slug]/page.tsx:55-58`; `realisations/[slug]/page.tsx:62-65`). `resolveProjectImage` (`src/lib/project-media.ts:5-9`) touches filesystem only for developer-controlled project media data; do not infer a request-path traversal without a new reachable writer. Video embeds (`src/lib/video.ts:5-12`) and Google Maps are browser-side integrations with static/developer content, not server-side fetch endpoints. No reachable XML parser, command runner, arbitrary outbound URL fetcher, dynamic evaluator, SQL/NoSQL client, or authenticated object storage API was found. Merely seeing unused argon2/notion packages or the old private-storage helper is not evidence those surfaces are reachable.

## Severity Calibration
Critical: demonstrated anonymous code execution or broad usable operator credential compromise through the local runtime; public marketing content and service listings do not count as sensitive data. High: validated access to confidential contact content or reusable mail-service credentials, or serious directly proven application compromise. Medium: demonstrated meaningful abuse of the server's mail authority, bounded sensitive action manipulation, or exploitable content injection requiring recipient interaction; missing rate limiting alone is not proof of these effects. Low/informational: public service/version metadata, stale robots exclusions, security headers, unattached unused helper concerns, and generic error behavior without restricted data. No session/account/tenant exists in observed runtime, so standard IDOR/JWT/CSRF account-takeover stories are inapplicable absent discovery of additional code. Attachment extension/MIME spoofing alone is not RCE because the live app only base64-encodes and emails bytes; concrete downstream execution or other unauthorized impact must be demonstrated. Any rate/size-related availability claim needs actual bounded impact evidence rather than speculative memory arithmetic.

## Local runtime preparation evidence
A loopback-only runtime is now available at `http://127.0.0.1:3100`, process PID `2199` (startup terminal session `11104`). It serves the existing Windows-generated `.next` production artifact through Next 16.4.3 `next start`; current-source/build parity remains unverified. GET `/api/health`, `/`, `/contact`, `/services`, `/realisations`, `/robots.txt`, and `/sitemap.xml` returned 200; `/about-us` returned local 308 redirect to `/a-propos`. Existing `.env` is not used for live mail: startup explicitly exported empty `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, and `CONTACT_EMAIL`; the source `sendContactEmails` checks empty API key before constructing Resend. This is application-level email suppression, not an OS network egress policy. Tests must not restart without those overrides. No product/config files were edited; Next auto-fetched Linux SWC because bundled node_modules initially contained Windows-only native dependencies. Shared runtime note `206290` records reproducible startup and gaps. Runtime source has no auth/database requiring account seeding.
